exceptions.reason: Concept r3 D1-D3/E1: widen the relation CHECK only by serves and asks_for; keep every existing event family, named type, actor exception, tenant boundary and node-reference check while adding goal events under visible-goal/outcome RLS. CREATE SEQUENCE goal_response_seq allocates response generations and rewrites no table. No backfill, sample rows or destructive data step. ALTER POLICY, CHECK replacement and CREATE SEQUENCE are outside the expand-safe allowlist. Exact bytes require coordinator cross-family review and whole-chain previous-binary compatibility/backup gates before merge or release. This artifact grants no acceptance, push or deployment authority. Round 2 isolates the identical goal-event invoker visibility checks in aeon_goal_event_visible to prevent recursive policy-plan expansion; it does not change accepted subjects, tenants, projects, actor exceptions or node-reference checks. Round 3 keeps the same invoker predicates while constraining goal/outcome identity probes and checking event references by indexed identity in aeon_event_refs_visible; this avoids hashing every visible outcome for a watermark. Null/empty reference arrays and every existing event family retain their prior semantics. Outcome serves visibility likewise checks at most twenty target identities without a correlated anti-join, retaining the cycle/depth guard and restoration of project visibility; event subjects use the same invoker identity helper. The non-outcome shortcut uses <> ALL with a statement-level ARRAY kind lookup, preserving the ordinary-kind selectivity instead of a whole-policy CASE estimate; outcome serves checks and visibility semantics stay unchanged. Fix4 adds the bounded invoker aeon_outcome_serves projection: authorize the outcome under the original project and rule policies once, then collect at most twenty-one serves targets under widened project visibility and restore it before returning or propagating an error. Outcome visibility already requires every target to be visible; tenant isolation is never widened. This removes per-edge recursive source checks without granting visibility to hidden outcomes or changing the existing relation policy. The released aeon_work_scope signature, invoker RLS, root/pair budgets, cycle termination, leaf semantics and result fields remain unchanged: visible adjacency is materialized before its recursive hash join, and parent probes use distinct node identities while all root/node pairs remain intact. This prevents the Goals policy from forcing repeated recursive joins and duplicate parent probes. No stored rows or schema columns change. Fix5 replaces tenant-wide adjacency with indexed child pages while retaining the work-scope signature and root/pair/cycle/leaf semantics. The additive goal_event_refs index projection stores immutable event/node/type/time metadata, is classified in the DSAR inventory, and applies both tenant RLS and the authoritative event visibility policy to every read. The invoker AFTER INSERT trigger supports previous writers; a tenant-fenced append-only backfill copies existing references without rewriting events or nodes. No node or event foreign key is added after the counter lock. Plain UUID/time keys avoid non-leakproof JSON/array scans under RLS. Bounded invoker reference and parent helpers support separate selected-range and recorded-prefix reads, and normalize before/after bulk and wrapped project edges without widening any existing visibility policy. Existing events remain the sole source of snapshots and values.
